title: Musculoskeletal System and Skin
tagline: Bones and joints, fractures, arthritis, connective-tissue disease, back pain and the skin
summary: Musculoskeletal and skin conditions are among the commonest reasons people see a doctor. This course covers bone and joint biology and examination, fractures, osteoarthritis, inflammatory and crystal arthritis, connective-tissue disease and vasculitis, back and neck pain, and the structure, common diseases and cancers of the skin.
overview: Back pain, a swollen knee, a rash, a broken wrist: musculoskeletal and skin problems are among the commonest reasons for consulting a doctor anywhere in the world, and most are managed by non-specialists. This course treats them as core clinical medicine. Each chapter starts from the biology of the tissue, moves to recognising patterns in the history and examination, and ends with investigation and management as set out in current guidance, mainly from NICE in the UK, with European and international criteria where they are the standard.

The first half follows the skeleton and its joints. It begins with bone as a living tissue (remodelling, calcium and bone density) and with the synovial joint and its examination, then covers fractures and how they heal, osteoarthritis as a disease of the whole joint, the inflammatory and crystal arthritides with their treat-to-target strategies, and the systemic autoimmune diseases and vasculitides, where clinical patterns and autoantibodies do the diagnostic work. A chapter on back and neck pain separates the common non-specific pain from radicular pain and the few serious causes, such as cauda equina syndrome, that must not be missed.

The last two chapters turn to the skin: its structure and barrier, how to describe what you see, and the common diseases (eczema, psoriasis, acne, urticaria, infections, drug eruptions and blistering disorders), then skin cancer, from ultraviolet DNA damage to the recognition, staging and modern treatment of melanoma. Quantitative threads run throughout: T-scores and adjusted calcium, interfragmentary strain and compartment pressures, DAS28 and classification scores, likelihood ratios for antibody and fluid tests, SCORTEN, and the arithmetic of ultraviolet dose and sunscreen.
outcomes: Describe the structure of bone and synovial joints and the cellular control of remodelling, and interpret bone biochemistry, DXA T-scores and synovial fluid analysis.
Take a focused musculoskeletal history and examination, distinguishing inflammatory from mechanical joint pain, and recognise a septic joint as an emergency.

Describe fractures accurately, explain the stages and mechanics of bone healing, outline the principles of fracture management, and recognise early and late complications, including compartment syndrome.
Explain the pathogenesis and risk factors of osteoarthritis and outline its diagnosis and management according to NICE guidance, including the indications for and complications of joint replacement.

Recognise rheumatoid arthritis, the spondyloarthritides, gout and calcium pyrophosphate deposition; apply classification criteria and disease activity scores; and explain treat-to-target management and the main drug classes.

Interpret autoantibody tests in the light of pretest probability, and recognise and outline the management of lupus, antiphospholipid syndrome, Sjögren's disease, systemic sclerosis, myositis, polymyalgia rheumatica, giant cell arteritis and the vasculitides.

Triage back and neck pain into non-specific, radicular and serious causes, examine the nerve roots, recognise cauda equina syndrome and metastatic cord compression, and outline management according to NICE NG59.

Describe skin structure and skin lesions, and outline the diagnosis and management of eczema, psoriasis, acne (including isotretinoin safeguards), urticaria, skin infections, severe drug reactions and blistering diseases.
Explain how ultraviolet radiation causes skin cancer, recognise keratinocyte cancers and melanoma, stage melanoma, outline its treatment, and give evidence-based prevention advice.

history.title: Fractures and dislocations in the Hippocratic texts
history.detail: The Hippocratic texts On Fractures and On Joints describe traction, reduction and splinting of fractures and the reduction of dislocated shoulders, manoeuvres still recognisable today.

history.title: A chimney sweep's cancer
history.detail: Percivall Pott links scrotal cancer in chimney sweeps to soot, the first recognition that an environmental exposure can cause cancer, and a skin cancer at that.

history.title: Paget's disease of bone
history.detail: Sir James Paget describes osteitis deformans, a disorder of excessive, disorganised bone remodelling in older adults, now known as Paget's disease of bone and treated with bisphosphonates.

history.title: Aspirin synthesised
history.detail: Felix Hoffmann at Bayer synthesises acetylsalicylic acid, marketed as aspirin in 1899: the first mass-produced synthetic anti-inflammatory drug, and the start of a century of work on cyclo-oxygenase and NSAIDs.

history.title: Rickets explained
history.detail: Edward Mellanby produces rickets in puppies by diet and cures it with cod-liver oil, identifying a dietary antirachitic factor and opening the path to vitamin D and the endocrine control of calcium and bone.

history.title: Cortisone for arthritis
history.detail: Philip Hench, Edward Kendall and colleagues at the Mayo Clinic report dramatic improvement of rheumatoid arthritis with cortisone. The relapses and toxicity that followed taught the lessons about glucocorticoids that every generation of rheumatologists relearns; Hench and Kendall shared the 1950 Nobel Prize with Tadeus Reichstein.

history.title: The Charnley total hip
history.detail: John Charnley at Wrightington Hospital combines a small metal femoral head, a high-density polyethylene cup, bone cement and clean-air theatres in his low-friction arthroplasty, making total hip replacement one of the most successful operations in medicine.

history.title: Methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis
history.detail: Michael Weinblatt and colleagues publish a controlled trial in the New England Journal of Medicine showing that low-dose weekly methotrexate reduces rheumatoid arthritis activity. It becomes the anchor drug of disease-modifying therapy and of the strategy of treating early.

history.title: Blocking TNF in rheumatoid arthritis
history.detail: Marc Feldmann, Ravinder Maini and colleagues show in a randomised trial that an antibody against tumour necrosis factor (later named infliximab) reduces rheumatoid arthritis activity. Biological therapy enters rheumatology, bringing with it the infection screening that now precedes every biologic.

history.title: Melanoma immunotherapy
history.detail: Ipilimumab, an antibody against CTLA-4 based on James Allison's research, becomes the first drug shown to prolong survival in metastatic melanoma; BRAF inhibitors are approved the same year, and the outlook for advanced melanoma changes completely.

references.title: Apley and Solomon's System of Orthopaedics and Trauma
references.authors: Ashley W. Blom, David Warwick and Michael R. Whitehouse (eds)
references.note: Tenth edition. The standard British orthopaedic textbook, clear on fracture description, healing, complications and joint replacement.

references.title: Oxford Textbook of Rheumatology
references.authors: Richard A. Watts, Philip G. Conaghan, Christopher Denton, Helen Foster, John Isaacs and Ulf Müller-Ladner (eds)
references.note: Fourth edition. A comprehensive reference for inflammatory arthritis, connective-tissue disease and vasculitis.

references.title: Rook's Textbook of Dermatology
references.authors: Christopher Griffiths, Jonathan Barker, Tanya Bleiker, Walayat Hussain and Rosalind Simpson (eds)
references.note: Tenth edition. The major reference work of British dermatology, for depth on any skin disease in this course.

references.title: Clinical Dermatology
references.authors: Richard B. Weller, Hamish J. A. Hunter and Margaret W. Mann
references.note: Fifth edition. A concise, well-illustrated introduction to skin disease for students and generalists.

references.title: Kumar and Clark's Clinical Medicine
references.authors: Adam Feather, David Randall and Mona Waterhouse (eds)
references.note: Tenth edition. The rheumatology and dermatology chapters give a compact clinical overview to read alongside this course.
